articles.headline: Packers' O-line leaves Jordan Love under constant pressure
articles.description: The Packers have allowed more "quick pressures" against Love than any team in the NFL -- and it's not close.
articles.headlineJa: パッカーズのOラインがジョーダン・ラブを常にプレッシャーに晒す
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズがラブに対して許した「クイックプレッシャー」の数はNFLのどのチームよりも多く、圧倒的な差となっている。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- When Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love said after last week's 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons that he needs to make quicker decisions, the next question should have been: How much quicker can he possibly make them given the light speed with which opposing pass rushers have been in his face?

According to Next Gen Stats, the Packers have allowed the most "quick pressures" -- defined as pressure on the quarterback in less than 2.5 seconds -- in the NFL, and it's not close. Love has been quick pressured 37 times in three games. No other team has allowed more than 28.

In last Thursday's loss, the Falcons recorded 15 quick pressures, second most in a game this season. The most was the 17 the Packers allowed to the Vikings in Week 1.

"Obviously you always need time," Love said Wednesday. "The more time you have, the better you're able to pick apart the defense and find those completions. That's with anything, you always want time. Obviously there's times you might not have time, you've got to find those answers.

"That's an area that we've got to improve on, in pass [protection], making sure we're going to the right people and sustaining blocks for as long as we can, give me some time to pick the defense apart and obviously something that we need to improve on."

At some point, the concern is the impact it will have on Love -- both from a fundamental standpoint and when it comes to his health -- if it hasn't already. The concern is that a quarterback who has been hit so many times can start to feel pressure even when it's not there, or as coaches and scouts call it, "seeing ghosts."

"There's definitely some plays, especially later in the [Falcons] game, where we talked about my feet are just getting a little bit off and that definitely is some of the pressure being a factor in that," Love said. "In that scenario, I've just got to be better right there.

"I can improve my game to make sure I'm staying on schedule, trusting my feet, reading with my feet, and it's going to help me be as accurate as possible. But I think it's a natural reaction sometimes as a quarterback, you might feel sped up. I've got to fight that urge and trust my feet and still be great in the pocket."

While Love has thrown for the fourth-most yards (844) through three games and has six touchdown passes against two interceptions, the problem is that he has a 1.7 QBR when pressured. That's the second lowest in the NFL ahead of Denver's Bo Nix (1.1). Love has a 31% completion rate, no touchdowns and both of his interceptions when pressured.

Teams might even try to send more rushers after Love. He ranks only 10th in pressure percentage this season, according to ESPN tracking, taking pressure on 38% of his dropbacks. However, that could be in part because he's averaging 2.49 seconds per pass, the quickest in the league according to Next Gen Stats. He averaged 2.84 seconds in his first three seasons as a starter.

articles.headline: Browns' QB situation takes a turn as Deshaun Watson finds his footing
articles.description: Cleveland's 2-1 start and the QB's late-game performances have helped to shift the conversation around the future of the position.
articles.headlineJa: デショーン・ワトソンが復調の兆しを見せ、ブラウンズのQB事情に変化
articles.descriptionJa: クリーブランドの2勝1敗のスタートと、試合終盤における同QBの活躍により、このポジションの将来を巡る議論の流れが変わりつつある。
articles.body:
DESHAUN WATSON JOGGED toward the tunnel leading to the Cleveland Browns' locker room at Huntington Bank Field surrounded by cheers last Sunday -- a stark contrast to the loud boos he received the last time he played in front of the hometown fans.

Waiting outside the locker room for the Browns' starting quarterback was general manager Andrew Berry, who smiled broadly. The two shared a handshake and hug. With Berry's arm around Watson's shoulder, they turned, ready to celebrate with the team.

The sequence leading to that scene and the change in reception from fans was a game-winning touchdown drive to defeat the Carolina Panthers 21-18 in Week 3. The win marked Watson's second fourth-quarter comeback in as many weeks, which seemed implausible after a late August preseason game, when Watson struggled in the second half, was loudly booed, and later lashed out at fans in the postgame news conference.

That preseason discontent seemed like the final chapter for a player who received a five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract in March 2022 but was crumbling under high expectations in Cleveland. Through four seasons, 19 mostly underwhelming performances were sandwiched between an 11-game suspension after more than two dozen women accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions, and multiple significant injuries since Cleveland traded three first-round picks to the Houston Texans for Watson.

Entering the 2026 season, the consensus view among Cleveland spectators was that the Browns might finally part ways with Watson at the end of the regular season, taking an exorbitant $86 million dead cap hit while possibly turning to the 2027 NFL draft -- with the Browns holding two first-round picks -- to solve the franchise's perpetual quarterback conundrum. Such a conclusion would render playing Watson pointless.

Instead, Watson emerged as the starter following a monthslong competition. His late-game performances and the Browns' 2-1 start have added another wrinkle to the NFL's most confounding quarterback dynamic: Cleveland enters its "Thursday Night Football" home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video) with first place in the AFC North on the line.

"[Watson] is playing pretty well. At least give him enough of a sample size to see what he can do," an NFC executive told ESPN.

While team sources indicated that Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced the Browns to consider Watson the long-term answer, Cleveland's surprising start has shifted the conversation inside the building to whether the 31-year-old passer and the Browns can build short-term momentum.

"I feel like I have a lot of football left in my game, in my career, and that's how I approach the game," Watson said last week. "That's how I approach my preparation on and off the field. I feel like I'm 10 years in, but still got a lot of football to play, definitely for myself."

articles.headline: Why Darnell Washington has become the Steelers' X factor
articles.description: At 6-foot-7 and nearly 300 pounds, the Pittsburgh tight end is more than a viral hurdle highlight reel.
articles.headlineJa: ダーネル・ワシントンがスティーラーズのXファクターとなった理由
articles.descriptionJa: 身長6フィート7インチ、体重約300ポンドを誇るピッツバーグのタイトエンドは、SNSで話題となった障害物跳びのハイライト動画以上の存在だ。
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Darnell Washington vividly remembers the youth football practice where he hurdled his first defender.

A perpetual outlier among his peers since a third-grade growth spurt, Washington towered over the defender opposite him in the Oklahoma drill. As he strategized his approach before the whistle, Washington got an idea.

"I'm going to just hurdle him," he thought.

And that's just what he did.

"It felt amazing just passing somebody without getting touched because I never juke, so I can't say, 'Oh, I juked somebody clean and just kept running,"' Washington said. "I know I don't do that. So even back then, it's a similar game plan, at least for me. Stiff arm, lower the shoulder or hurdle."

Nearly two decades later, Washington's size advantage and moves are the same, but the stage is not. Now checking in at 6-foot-7 and officially listed at 264 pounds, but realistically closer to 300 pounds, the Pittsburgh Steelers tight end is making a name for himself with highlight-reel hurdles and stiff arms against the unlucky defensive backs tasked with slowing him down.

Thursday night, the 25-year-old will have an opportunity to add another chapter to his legendary lore in the Steelers' first primetime matchup of the season against the Cleveland Browns (8:15 ET, Amazon Prime).

Washington, though, is more than a viral clip. He's the X factor of the Steelers offense as a sure-handed pass catcher, practically untackleable runner and selfless blocker.

The stats support Washington's impact, too. The Steelers are 13-2 when Washington plays at least 40 offensive snaps. When he plays fewer than 40 snaps on offense, the team's record drops to 18-22. Perhaps it's not a coincidence that Washington played 47 snaps in the Steelers' 30-27 Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals.

And as coach Mike McCarthy watched Washington turn one of those snaps into a 47-yard path of destruction with Bengals defenders trailing helplessly behind him, the Steelers coach had one thought: "Why don't you give him the ball more?" McCarthy said Monday afternoon, laughing as he thought back to that moment. "I think that's probably what everybody else is saying. He's unique. You can see it, and it seems like it's always on the sideline. He's a hard guy to tackle. I mean, he's a tough matchup."

That has been the case since former Desert Pines (Las Vegas) High School coach Tico Rodriguez first noticed Washington playing wide receiver for a different school in a 7-on-7 tournament in the summer of 2017, just after Washington's freshman year.

"He was very coordinated for his size," Rodriguez said. "And I was just like, 'Wow, this coach is very lucky to have him.'"

Three weeks later, Washington unexpectedly walked into the weight room at Desert Pines.

"He had just moved into our area, and my prayers had been answered," Rodriguez said. "He just walked in, 6-6, 220 and I was like, 'Wow.' It was a perfect fit for him to be here with us."

articles.headline: Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled
articles.description: Whenever LaLiga rivals Barcelona and Real Madrid clash, the world watches. So it's only fitting that El Clásico gets its own bespoke match ball.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナ対レアル・マドリードのラ・リーガ「クラシコ」専用試合球が公開
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのライバルであるバルセロナとレアル・マドリードが激突する時、世界中が注目する。それだけに、エル・クラシコのために専用の特別試合球が用意されるのはまさに相応しい。
articles.body:
Whenever bitter LaLiga rivals Barcelona and Real Madrid clash in El Clásico, it's a match that the world watches.

The next time that happens will be later this month, when Barça host Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25 (stream the match LIVE on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

But, just to add a little extra luster to a fixture that is already positively dripping in it, Puma has revealed their new bespoke match ball that is to be used for the two league meetings between Spanish football's twin heavyweights.

For the second year running, Puma has designed a special "ELCLASICO" ball which combines eye-catching colours and retro-tinged graphics to herald the monumental contest.

White with flashes of gold and black, the new ball is a custom variant of the official LaLiga 2026-27 match ball -- the Stellar Nitro Ultimate. It is an updated version of the inaugural Puma ELCLASICO model, a ball which was first used in October 2025.

On that day, Madrid beat Barça 2-1 at the Bernabéu thanks to goals from Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham. However, Madrid coach Xabi Alonso was fired three months later, and Barça had the last laugh as they retained their LaLiga crown and helped consign their rivals to a second consecutive season without a major trophy.

Barça have made a flying start to the 2026-27 season, winning all seven of their league games so far and scoring 31 along the way. Madrid are six points and three points below them in the table, so they will already be facing a crucial point in their season when they travel to Catalonia in just over three weeks' time.

articles.headline: Premier League 'dragged through the mud' by Man City case - Gary Neville
articles.description: The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグはマンCの件で「泥を塗られた」― ゲイリー・ネヴィル
articles.descriptionJa: ゲイリー・ネヴィル氏は、マンチェスター・シティの有罪判決によってプレミアリーグが「泥を塗られた」と述べた。
articles.body:
The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.

An independent commission found City guilty on all charges related to breaching Premier League financial rules, concluding they "clearly intended to circumvent" the regulations over a period of nine seasons, primarily by disguising owner funding as sponsorship revenue.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has called on the club's owner Sheikh Mansour to sell up, while former Manchester United full-back Neville believes the reputation of the whole league has been affected.

"To listen to this, it is chilling," he said on the Stick To Football podcast.

 

"We always think that we've got an enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard, and that it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match-fixing, referee scandals.

"This is now coming to our country. This is now coming to our league. This is the greatest export that we have in our country. At the moment we're being dragged through the mud."

City were found to have inflated revenue and hid costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season period, and in doing so avoided breaching Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Man City should be stripped of titles - Jamie Carragher

- Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?

They have indicated their intention to appeal against the commission's decision, saying it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City said "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all [the club's] positions."

Neville described the "irrefutable evidence" remark as "bizarre," adding: "It was a bit Trump-esque, wasn't it?"

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ロジャースの2026年NFLシーズン：記録とマイルストーンを追う
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズのQBはNFL22年目のシーズンで記録更新に挑んでおり、ESPNは彼の「最後の挑戦」を記録している。
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 3 he has appeared in 290), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 3, he has 531) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 3, he needs 3,026 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INTs, 0 sacks, 0 rushes

Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

Week 1: Steelers 20, Falcons 13

Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard

Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the Green Bay Packers, per ESPN Research.

articles.headline: Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher
articles.description: Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.
articles.headlineJa: マンCオーナーは「有罪の恥」からクラブを売却すべき＝ジェイミー・キャラガー氏
articles.descriptionJa: 元リヴァプールのディフェンダー、ジェイミー・キャラガー氏によると、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反による有罪判決を受け、マンチェスター・シティのオーナー陣はクラブを手放さなければならないという。
articles.body:
Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.

Carragher says there can be no future for any executives implicated in the scandal, which City have stressed they intend to appeal, from majority owner Sheikh Mansour downwards.

An independent commission concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs through a series of "sham" commercial deals over a nine-season period.

Writing in the Daily Telegraph, Carragher said: "Manchester City are the end of their Abu Dhabi era. The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up.

"There is no way to sugar-coat this. The scale of the institutional cheating and lack of co-operation in the investigation means the position of all City executives involved is untenable.

"Fighting on will only prolong the agony of supporters who wrong believe their pleas of innocence."

Carragher's views appear to contradict those of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who suggested on Wednesday that such a sanction may not be suited to a group who have pumped billions into the club since their arrival in the city in 2008.

Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, told the BBC: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

Burnham's comments came after David Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) said the ruling "raises serious issues" and pointed out the body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives once proceedings come to a close.

Carragher is adamant there must be no mercy shown to those proven to have been complicit in one of the game's greatest controversies, and that any failure to uphold the rules will render such powers obsolete.

He added: "The Premier League's owners' and directors' test makes clear the repercussions for breaking the fundamental rules that all member clubs, including City, established and signed up to.

"Anyone who falls short must be disqualified from being Premier League directors and owners; otherwise, the regulations are not fit for purpose."

City have shown every intention of rigorously contesting the charges, and in a further development on Wednesday, the club's main sponsor Etihad Airways released a statement saying it was assessing its legal options following the independent commission's ruling.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: インターナショナルブレイク中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初のインターナショナルブレイク期間中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースと情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Premier League depth charts for most popular teams: Who is key?
articles.description: The Premier League is well underway, but with the transfer window closed, where do players stand in their teams? How deep do the squads go?
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ人気クラブの選手層一覧：鍵を握るのは誰？
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグは本格的に進行中ですが、移籍市場が閉じた今、各選手はチーム内でどのような立ち位置にいるのでしょうか？各クラブの選手層の厚さを検証します。
articles.body:
The Premier League season is five games in, and with the transfer window closed until Jan. 1, there will be no more incomings or outgoings (unless a free agent can be snapped up.)

As teams start to hit their stride and summer additions become accustomed to their surroundings, it's time to take a look at where the players stand with their respective squads.

Here are depth charts of the best options for the first XI and backup XI for the six most-followed clubs in the league. Of course, it's hard to predict who could be called upon as the fixtures pile up, but this should give you an idea of how strong each team is.

(Note: Each player appears in the main squad list once, even if he could fit into multiple spots. We have also included injured players, although those likely to be out for the season are noted separately.)

ARSENAL

Goalkeeper: David Raya, Kepa Arrizabalaga, Illan Meslier

Right back: Jurriën Timber, Ben White

Left back: Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapié,

Center back: William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Cristhian Mosquera, Ezri Konsa

Central midfield: Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi, Bruno Guimarães, Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly

Attacking midfield/Forward: Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze, Martin Ødegaard, 

Striker: Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyökeres

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Raya

Timber, Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Calafiori

Rice, Guimarães

Saka, Ødegaard, Tzolis

Havertz

SECOND XI (4-3-3)

Kepa

White, Konsa, Mosquera, Hincapié

Lewis-Skelly, Merino

Madueke, Eze, Dowman

Gyökeres

EXTRAS: Meslier, Zubimendi

Arsenal came out of the summer window having executed their plans well. Those who departed were moved out largely on the club's terms, while the arrivals were clearly targeted according to specific requirements. The only slightly ambiguous outcome is that with the additions of defender Konsa and midfielder Guimarães, the Premier League champions have strengthened a core that was already exceptionally strong; Arteta might have to call on his man-management skills to keep certain players happy.

Konsa adds depth to an already impressive defense in the wake of an injury to William Saliba, while Guimarães does the same to central midfield as Zubimendi and Merino struggled for form and fitness respectively.

In attack, the club went through a mini-revamp. Four first-team players left -- Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona), Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Gabriel Martinelli (Al Hilal) and Ethan Nwaneri (loan, Dortmund) -- while only one, Tzolis, arrived. The Greece international has made an encouraging start and gives Arteta a different option from the left, with a superb right foot and set-piece expertise, and while Eze and Madueke can deputize there, Tzolis is the only specialist in the role. Using either of the former two on the left may also reduce the cover available elsewhere, particularly for the injury-prone Ødegaard. articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye former Liverpool defender Quansah
articles.description: Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍噂・ニュース：レアル・マドリードが元リヴァプールのDFクアンサーに注目
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは来夏に向けてバイエル・レバークーゼンのDFジャレル・クアンサーの動向を追跡しています。「Transfer Talk」が最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah is on the radar of Real Madrid ahead of next summer, while Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer, according to Bild. Los Blancos have scouted the 23-year-old England international as they look to add at least two defensive additions to their squad, following his solid displays in Germany since moving from Liverpool for €35 million in 2025, while previous suitors Arsenal are also monitoring developments.

- Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea are actively monitoring the France international, with Xabi Alonso keen on reinforcing his options at right back and the Spanish club looking to raise money to fund their new signings.

- Tottenham Hotspur have added Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to their shortlist of future goalkeeping targets alongside Brighton's Bart Verbruggen, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Greece international has impressed so far, with three clean sheets in five Premier League appearances following his £20 million summer move from Olympiakos.

- Bournemouth will not entertain January offers to sign England midfielder Alex Scott despite interest from Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea, reports BBC Sport. The Cherries intend to hold on to the 23-year-old until at least next summer as he enters the final two years of his contract, with transfer valuation of at least £100 million in their minds.

- Real Madrid striker Endrick could face another loan move in January due to a lack of playing time, according to Diario AS.
